risks: Low. Interviews may touch on distressing symptoms or on feeling ignored; interviewers can pause, and a triage nurse is available if a current symptom is disclosed. Nurses may fear blame for slow responses, so results are reported by shift pattern, never by named nurse.
consent: Written or recorded verbal consent for interviews, with information in the patient's preferred language; platform and triage data are used under the approved evaluation, and patients can ask for their data to be excluded.
data: Exports are pseudonymised by the informatics lead before analysis; interview recordings are transcribed, de-identified and deleted after checking; data stay on the centre's research drive under REB-ONC-2026-044 and DA-2026-17.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: older patients, people in the most deprived areas, those without home internet and those needing an interpreter are the groups most likely to stop reporting and the least heard in the evidence. The sample deliberately includes them, interviews use professional interpreters, and completion is reported by age, deprivation and preferred language.
effectiveness: The evaluation shows where the reporting loop breaks and for whom; it does not re-estimate effectiveness, which trials have addressed.
efficiency: Uses existing exports and one protected day a week; interviews by telephone limit travel for patients on treatment.
costs: Interpreter fees and transcription, met from the unit's education budget; no other costs.
grants: None needed; the joint display could support a later bid to test a response standard across the network.
partnerships: Triage nurses, the rollout committee, the platform's informatics lead and two patient partners who stopped reporting during their own treatment.
rebPath: Approved by the research ethics board on 2026-09-02 (REB-ONC-2026-044), covering platform data and interviews; any change to the interview guide goes back as an amendment.
limitations: Two clinics; confounding by illness severity in the mechanism analysis; interview views may not transfer to the lung and head-and-neck clinics.
summary: Approved low-risk evaluation with deliberate inclusion of the patients most likely to stop reporting.
